title: DECISION: qty: counts copies per-printing (SETTLED)
description:
qty:/count: must count copies of the SAME printing (card_id + variant + language), NOT aggregated across a card's printings.

Worked example (from the user): owning 2x Base Set Pikachu (same printing) + 1x Base Set 2 Pikachu satisfies 'pikachu qty:2' ONLY for the Base Set copy; the Base Set 2 copy (qty 1) does not match.

DECIDED: per-printing. Implementation: correlated subquery (SELECT count(*) FROM collection c2 WHERE c2.printing_id = c.printing_id) <op> N. is:dupe = that count >= 2. In catalog-wide mode an unowned printing has count 0.
design: Avoids GROUP BY/HAVING restructuring of the row query; the correlated subquery composes cleanly into the WHERE clause.
close_reason: Decided: qty: counts copies per-printing (card_id+variant+language) via correlated subquery; is:dupe = count>=2. Confirmed by user with the Base Set vs Base Set 2 Pikachu example.

title: DECISION: Owned-aware SearchRow shape + catalog-wide LEFT-JOIN template
description:
Current CollectionRow.id is non-optional and the query is FROM collection c JOIN printings. For is:missing/is:unowned the result includes catalog cards with no collection row.

PROPOSAL: add a new SearchRow type = CollectionRow fields made Optional where collection-specific (id, condition, status, acquired_at, binder/deck...) + owned: bool. Compiler emits two _build_full_sql templates: (a) OWNED mode FROM collection c JOIN (printings UNION user_printings) ... default status owned+ordered; (b) CATALOG-WIDE mode FROM cards JOIN printings LEFT JOIN collection, owned = CASE WHEN c.id IS NOT NULL. Mode chosen by presence of is:missing/is:unowned/is:owned. Ratify the row shape + the trigger rule.
design: Reuse existing ROW_COLUMNS_SQL/ROW_FROM where possible. ts-rs export SearchRow for the frontend. Frontend renders unowned slots dimmed (like deprecated variants).
notes:
RATIFIED. Row shape = new SearchRow (NOT a retrofit of CollectionRow, which stays as-is for list_by_binder/deck/order/get_row).

GRANULARITY (user decision): ONE ROW PER PRINTING in ALL modes (unified). Every printing in the catalog is a candidate row; owned_count tells you how many copies you have (0 = missing, rendered dimmed). Per-copy detail (condition/status/binder/deck/purchase_price/acquired_at/graded, with collection.id) moves into an expand/drill-down, NOT top-level rows.

SearchRow fields: printing_id, card_id, set_code, set_name, set_ptcgo_code, set_symbol_url, number, name, rarity, artist, supertype, subtypes, types, attacks, market_price, image_small, variant, variant_description, owned: bool, owned_count: i64, and copies: Vec<CopySummary> (id, condition, language, status, graded, purchase_price, acquired_at, binder_id, deck_id) — recommend attaching copies inline via a grouped second query to avoid N+1; lazy-fetch-on-expand is the fallback.

SQL: two templates, both per-printing.
  OWNED MODE (default, no ownership flag): FROM (printings ⋃ user_printings) p JOIN cards JOIN sets, owned_count via correlated count over collection; default status owned+ordered applied as an EXISTS over copies.
  CATALOG-WIDE MODE (is:missing/is:unowned/is:owned present): same FROM but LEFT JOIN collection; is:missing -> owned_count=0; is:owned -> owned_count>0.

COLLECTION-PREDICATE SEMANTICS in the per-printing model: status/condition/binder/deck/added/price/source/tag/note/graded compile to EXISTS (printing matches if >=1 copy satisfies). owned_count = TOTAL copies of the printing (not just matching copies). qty:/is:dupe count total copies per printing (D4). [Nuance deferred: 'count only matching copies' — revisit if needed.]
close_reason: Decided: new SearchRow type; one row per printing in all modes (unified); per-copy detail via expand; two per-printing SQL templates (owned INNER-ish / catalog-wide LEFT JOIN); collection predicates use EXISTS-over-copies semantics.

title: DECISION: Keyword registry as data (table+seed) vs Rust constants
description:
DeckDumpster's keywords.py holds the alias map, operator sets, color/rarity/status enums as in-code dicts. That is exactly the data-living-in-code smell this project flags (see memory data-model-is-the-product-...).

PROPOSAL (recommended): keyword definitions live in data/search_keywords.json -> a shared.sqlite 'search_keywords' table, seeded at pkdump setup like data/variants.json. Each row: canonical name, aliases, allowed operators, value-domain/enum ref, target column or JSON path, semantics tag. The pure core parser takes a &KeywordRegistry argument (loaded from DB at server start; from seed JSON in tests) so pkdump-core stays IO-free. Bonus: autocomplete + help page render from the same table (no hardcoded keyword list like DD's frontend).

Tension to resolve: parser needs alias->canonical at parse time, but core has no DB. Resolution = registry injected as a parameter. Ratify this approach (or choose constants).
design: Registry loaded once at server startup and cached in AppState; tests load from the JSON seed directly. Value enums (energy types, conditions, statuses, is-flags) either as columns on search_keywords or sibling seed tables.
notes: RATIFIED: data-driven. Keyword definitions live in data/search_keywords.json -> shared 'search_keywords' table, seeded at pkdump setup like variants.json. Pure core parser takes &KeywordRegistry (loaded from DB at server start; from JSON in tests). Autocomplete + help render from the same table.
close_reason: Decided: data-driven registry (table + seed JSON), registry injected into the pure parser. Unblocks idf.5/idf.6.

title: DECISION: Rarity ordering rank table for Pokemon rarities
description:
Pokemon rarity is dozens of unordered era-dependent strings ('Rare Holo','Illustration Rare','Special Illustration Rare','Double Rare','Common',...). There is no clean total order, so r>=rare / r<rare are ill-defined out of the box.

PROPOSAL (recommended): data/rarities.json -> shared 'rarities' table mapping {name, rank, group}. Gives a curated ordinal so r>=X works, plus rarity GROUPS (e.g. 'secret','ultra') as queryable aliases. Until ratified, r: and r= do exact/substring match only. Decide rank ordering and group taxonomy.
design: Same seed-at-setup pattern as variants.json. Compiler maps r: '=' to exact match and r>=/r< to a CASE/JOIN against rarities.rank.
notes: RATIFIED: yes, rank table. data/rarities.json -> shared 'rarities' table {name, rank, group}. Enables r>=/r< ordinal compares and rarity-group aliases. Rank ordering + group taxonomy to be authored in idf.6.
close_reason: Decided: add a curated rarities rank table (data-driven, same seed pattern). Unblocks idf.6.

title: WotC-era multi-print coverage: Shadowless group + group-aware sub_types
description:
## Problem

Base Set, Jungle, Fossil, Team Rocket, Gym Heroes/Challenge, and the Neo
sets all shipped multiple physical print runs per card (1st Edition vs
Unlimited; Base Set adds Shadowless on top). Our DB only produces ~1
active printing per card for these sets, so the binder-page browse view
collapses them into a single slot.

Concrete miss for Base Set (base1): TCGCSV models the set as two groups —
604 "Base Set" (Unlimited; sub_types Normal/Holofoil) and 1663 "Base Set
(Shadowless)" (sub_types Normal, 1st Edition, 1st Edition Holofoil,
Unlimited, Unlimited Holofoil). Group 1663's 102 products are downloaded
into tcgcsv_products but never joined to any set, because
sets.tcgcsv_group_id is a single column. Machamp is the lone accidental
first_ed_holo printing in base1 — it leaked in via the deck-exclusives
group (1840 / 2-Player Starter Set), not by design.

Concrete miss for Jungle/Fossil/etc.: their non-holo commons carry
subTypeName values "1st Edition" and "Unlimited" (plain, no "Holofoil"
suffix). pkdump-core sub_type_to_variant only recognizes "1st Edition
Holofoil" / "Unlimited Holofoil", so plain "1st Edition" / "Unlimited"
rows fall through to None and are silently dropped. Visible at e.g.
base2-46 Diglett: upstream offers both 1st Edition and Unlimited sub_types,
we keep neither and fabricate a single "normal" printing.

## Where the code is

- crates/pkdump-ingest/src/overrides.rs:228 — variants_from_tcgcsv
  joins sets.tcgcsv_group_id = tcgcsv_products.group_id (one group per set).
- crates/pkdump-core/src/variant.rs:60 — sub_type_to_variant is a flat
  match with no group context; it can't distinguish "Unlimited Holofoil"
  in group 604 (Unlimited-with-shadow) from the same string in group 1663
  (Shadowless-no-stamp).
- shared.sqlite sets schema — sets.tcgcsv_group_id is a single nullable
  column with UNIQUE constraint. No bridge table today.

## Colloquialism note

"Shadowless" at TCGplayer's productId level means cards lacking the right-side
art-frame shadow, which encompasses BOTH 1st-Edition-stamped prints AND
the brief unstamped Unlimited transition run. The 1st-Ed vs no-stamp
distinction is encoded in subTypeName only. There is no "Base Set 1st
Edition" group; 1st Edition is always a sub_type, never a group.

## What needs to be decided

1. Schema for set ↔ TCGCSV-group mapping (1:N).
2. Variant taxonomy additions and the group-aware sub_type mapping table.
3. Migration approach: how existing base1 printings reconcile with the
   new variants (the current base1 "holo"/"normal" rows ARE the Unlimited-
   with-shadow run; new shadowless_* and first_ed_* rows are additions,
   not renames).

## Scope check

Modern sets (SV / SWSH / SM / XY / BW / HGSS / DP / EX) are unaffected —
they're a single group each with sub_types our mapper already covers.
This issue is bounded to WotC-era (pre-EX-Ruby/Sapphire) and specifically
to the 7-set WotC original-block era plus Base Set 2 and Legendary
Collection.

## Acceptance

- base1 produces 5–6 active variant rows per holo Pokémon card (holo,
  shadowless_holo, first_ed_holo) and 3 for commons (normal,
  shadowless_normal, first_ed_normal).
- Jungle non-holo commons produce first_ed_normal + unlimited_normal.
- The user can enter their Base Set physical cards distinguishing
  1st Ed / Shadowless / Unlimited from the browse grid.
- No regressions on any modern set.

## References

- Discussion: this conversation, 2026-05-28.
- Schema proposal to be appended to this issue's --design once approved.
design:
## Implemented schema (V7__wotc_multiprint.sql)

### Bridge: 1:N set → groups via tcgplayer_groups
- Drop `sets.tcgcsv_group_id`. `tcgplayer_groups.set_code` is the bridge.
- Add `tcgplayer_groups.role` (NOT NULL DEFAULT 'primary'). Values today: 'primary' | 'shadowless'.
- Bridge JSON entries (data/overrides/tcgcsv_set_bridges.json) gain `role` field (defaults to 'primary'). Primary-role bridges wipe any conflicting auto-link to the same set_code; aux-role bridges layer on top without wiping. Added entry: (1663, base1, role=shadowless).

### Variant taxonomy + tiebreak
- Add `variants.tiebreak INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`. Sorts within rank.
- data/variants.json: added shadowless_normal (rank 0, tiebreak 1, color #e8e3d5), shadowless_holo (rank 1, tiebreak 1, color #e8e3d5), unlimited_normal (rank 0, tiebreak 2, color #8a7150). Tiebreaks on first_ed_* (0), shadowless_* (1), normal/unlimited_* (2).
- Variant struct + Variant.ts gain tiebreak field. New variantSortCmp() helper handles (rank, tiebreak, code); all three frontend sort sites switched to it.

### Group-aware sub_type → variant lookup table
- New table `tcgcsv_sub_type_variant_map(tcgcsv_group_id INTEGER, sub_type_name TEXT, variant_code TEXT REFERENCES variants(code), PRIMARY KEY(group_id, sub_type_name))`. group_id=0 is the global default sentinel.
- New module pkdump-db::sub_type_map: struct SubTypeVariantMap with .lookup(group_id, sub_type) — group-specific row first, falls back to (0, sub_type).
- New seed data/tcgcsv_sub_type_variants.json. Rules:
  - 0 (global): six base mappings the old flat sub_type_to_variant covered.
  - 604 (Base Set Unlimited): Normal/Holofoil → normal/holo (Unlimited-with-shadow).
  - 1663 (Base Set Shadowless): 1st Edition* → first_ed_*; Unlimited*/Normal/Holofoil → shadowless_*.
  - 635/630/605/1373/1441/1440/1396/1434/1389/1444/1374 (Jungle/Fossil/etc.): plain 1st Edition → first_ed_normal; plain Unlimited → unlimited_normal (the old Rust mapper dropped these).
- Deleted pkdump-core::variant::sub_type_to_variant; its callers in pkdump-ingest::overrides switched to the SubTypeVariantMap loaded once at expand_all_printings entry.
- Reconcile pass (sub_type_map::reconcile) wired into both `pkdump setup` and `pkdump data refresh`, matching the variants::reconcile pattern.

### Migration mechanics
- PRAGMA foreign_keys is OFF during refinery's run (set in pkdump-db::connection::open_shared, restored after). `defer_foreign_keys` doesn't apply to DDL like DROP TABLE — needed real OFF for the sets table rebuild because cards.set_code etc. hold FKs into sets.

### Variant expansion JOIN
- variants_from_tcgcsv now JOINs tcgcsv_products on tcgplayer_groups.set_code = ?1, iterating every group bridged to a set, not just the (formerly unique) primary group.

## New ops affordance
- `pkdump data expand` — runs only the variants + sub_type_map reconcile + variant expansion. No network. Used to validate this migration against the prod snapshot end-to-end.

## Verification (prod snapshot, 2026-05-28)

| card | active variants |
|---|---|
| base1-4 Charizard (Holo Rare) | holo, first_ed_holo, shadowless_holo, black_dot_error |
| base1-8 Machamp (Holo Rare, 1st-Ed-only) | first_ed_holo (group 1840 Starter Set source — correct; Machamp had no Base Set Unlimited or Shadowless print) |
| base1-44 Bulbasaur (Common) | normal, first_ed_normal, shadowless_normal |
| base2-46 Diglett (Jungle Common) | first_ed_normal, unlimited_normal (regression fix) |

base1 total active printings: 15 holo + 15 first_ed_holo + 15 shadowless_holo + 86 normal + 86 first_ed_normal + 86 shadowless_normal + 1 black_dot_error = 304, up from the previous 103.

## Tests
- 2 fail-first tests added in pkdump-ingest::overrides::tests:
  - base_set_charizard_splits_into_holo_first_ed_holo_and_shadowless_holo
  - jungle_non_holo_splits_into_first_ed_normal_and_unlimited_normal
- 4 new tests in pkdump-db::sub_type_map covering reconcile idempotency, global-default fallback, group-specific override priority, unknown-sub_type behavior.
- All existing tests (variants + ingest + server) green.
acceptance_criteria: base1 holo cards have 3 active variants (holo+shadowless_holo+first_ed_holo); base1 non-holos have 3 (normal+shadowless_normal+first_ed_normal); Jungle/Fossil non-holos split into first_ed_normal+unlimited_normal; no regressions on modern sets
close_reason: V7 migration + data table moves landed; group-aware sub_type_variant_map replaces the flat Rust mapper. Base Set splits into holo/first_ed_holo/shadowless_holo, Jungle/Fossil etc. split into first_ed_normal+unlimited_normal. Verified against prod snapshot (base1 103→304 active printings).

title: TCGCSV-first variant expansion (schema + algorithm rework, full reset)
description:
Take TCGCSV as the authoritative source for which printings a card has, instead of bootstrapping from pokemontcg.io price keys + rarity heuristics. Audit showed 130+ fabricated reverse_holo printings in ASC alone and BLK cards with non-existent 'normal' printings.

Bigger goal (added per user feedback): no conditional logic in the application to compensate for a bad data model or shitty data. The right answer is to make the data right and let the SQL queries be straightforward.

Schema changes (edit V1 directly — user has authorized a full wipe, no migration history to preserve):
1. New tcgcsv_products table: (product_id PK, group_id, name, collector_number, derived_variant). Populated by import_tcgcsv so expansion can query the full product list without holding it in memory.
2. printings gets a sub_type_name column. Set at expansion time from the TCGplayer sub_type the variant maps to. Price queries then become a simple JOIN — no CASE expressions, no IS NULL OR fallbacks.

Algorithm:
- import_tcgcsv runs BEFORE variant expansion and persists products + prices.
- derive_variants_from_tcgcsv(card): for the card's set group + collector number, list TCGCSV products. For each base product, emit one printing per advertised sub_type (Normal → normal, Reverse Holofoil → reverse_holo, Holofoil → holo, ...). For each pattern product (Master Ball / Energy Symbol / etc.), emit one printing of that pattern variant. Each printing knows its product_id and its sub_type_name.
- expand_all_printings: TCGCSV-derived first; if a card has no TCGCSV products (brand-new set TCGCSV hasn't fetched), fall back to a minimal 'just normal' bootstrap. Layer-3 overlay still applies on top for true exceptions (stamps, manual additions).

Code to delete:
- VARIANT_PRICE_SUBTYPE CASE constant (no longer needed once printings carry sub_type_name).
- IS NULL OR sub_type filter pattern at each call site.
- bootstrap_from_rarity's release_date pre-LC reverse-holo check (TCGCSV tells us what exists, not the year).
- variant_from_product_name + auto-create logic in link_card_printings — gets pulled into the new derive step.

Process:
1. V1 migration: add tcgcsv_products, add sub_type_name to printings.
2. Implement derive_variants_from_tcgcsv + new expand_all_printings.
3. Reorder data.rs refresh: TCGCSV first, then expand.
4. Simplify all price subqueries.
5. Tests: ASC patterns (Energy Symbol/Quick Ball); ASC C/U/R that should NOT get plain RH; BLK with no Normal sub_type; pre-LC commons; overlay still wins.
6. Teardown prod volume + reseed; spot-check ASC Dreepy, BLK Klink, 151 Bulbasaur, WHT Swadloon, base1 commons.

Per-keyword compilation for the full map (name/set/rarity/type/supertype/subtype/hp/artist/flavor/oracle-text/abilities/attacks/damage/retreat/weak/resist/dex/regulation/year/legalities/variant/is-flags/status/condition/grade/price/added/deck/binder/lang/source/tag/note/qty). qty: per-printing correlated subquery (D4). Lazy needs_*_join flags; order:/dir: extracted out of WHERE. 1=0 sentinel for parses-but-unsupported. Two _build_full_sql templates (owned INNER vs catalog-wide LEFT JOIN) + owned-aware SearchRow per D3. Unit tests: SQL substrings + bound params + execute against in-memory schema (mirror tests/test_search_compiler.py).
notes: Per D3 (unified per-printing): emit ONE ROW PER PRINTING in both templates. Collection-row predicates (status/condition/binder/deck/added/price/source/tag/note/graded) compile to EXISTS over the printing's copies; owned_count = total copies; qty:/is:dupe per-printing (D4). Build a new SearchRow (+ CopySummary) type rather than reusing CollectionRow. Attach copies inline via a grouped query (preferred) or lazy endpoint.

title: Keyword registry as data: seed JSON + tables + ingest seeding + DB loader
description: Create data/search_keywords.json (and data/rarities.json per D2, + is-flag definitions). Add search_keywords + rarities tables to schema_shared.sql (CREATE IF NOT EXISTS). Seed them in pkdump-ingest at pkdump setup, same pattern as variants.json. Add a pkdump-db loader that builds a KeywordRegistry from the tables (and a from-JSON path for tests). The registry feeds the parser (T1), the compiler (T3), and the autocomplete/help endpoints (T6). Populate the full Pokemon keyword map from the plan.

title: Core grammar/parser: lexer + AST + recursive-descent + QueryError
description: Port DeckDumpster's grammar.py + transformer.py + ast_nodes.py to pkdump-core/src/query/{lexer,ast,parser,registry,error}.rs. Pure, no IO. Ordered-regex tokenizer (handles -negation vs hyphen-in-name, : vs space, or/and as keywords-between-clauses). Recursive descent OR<AND(implicit)<NOT<atom. AST: And/Or/Not/Comparison/NameSearch/ExactName. Alias resolution against an injected &KeywordRegistry (per D1). QueryError carries a byte position for caret placement. Unit tests assert AST shape (mirror tests/test_search_parser.py).

title: Scryfall-style collection search query language
description:
Build a Scryfall/DeckDumpster-style search query language for the collection, ported from DeckDumpster's MTG implementation (vendored at _deckdumpster-src) to this Rust/SQLite/Svelte app.

Four-stage pipeline: ordered-regex lexer -> recursive-descent parser -> AST -> SQL compiler. Re-homed to crate boundaries: pure parser in pkdump-core/src/query/, compiler in pkdump-db/src/search.rs, route in pkdump-server. The keyword registry is DATA not code (search_keywords table seeded from data/search_keywords.json), following the data-model-is-the-product principle.

Surface decision: AUGMENT THE COLLECTION PAGE. The page moves from load-everything-then-filter-client-side (collection::list_rows) to a server-side query. is:missing/is:unowned flips the query catalog-wide so search operates cleanly over owned AND unowned cards (the headline requirement).

Coverage (v1): name, set (s:pfl via ptcgo_code), rarity, energy type (t:), supertype/subtype, hp, artist, flavor, abilities/attacks text, price/dates/quantity, is:missing PLUS variant-aware flags, grading+condition, attack/ability internals (damage/retreat/weakness/resistance), and dex#/regulation.

Test strategy (all four tiers, DeckDumpster's approach): (1) curated corpus, (2) parser/compiler unit tests, (3) generative reverse-parser fuzzing (always-on, offline), (4) pokemontcg.io differential oracle (opt-in, cached, with a grammar->Lucene translator for the card-metadata subset).

Reference reading: _deckdumpster-src/mtg_collector/search/{grammar,transformer,ast_nodes,keywords,compiler}.py and _deckdumpster-src/tests/{test_search_*,search_helpers/*}. Design record to be written at architecture/SEARCH_QUERY_LANGUAGE.md.

title: Set-stats 'Full set' value sums all print runs (WOTC ~$28k)
description: analytics() computed market_value as SUM over every non-deprecated printing in the set. WOTC sets print each card in three runs (1st Edition / Shadowless / Unlimited) and modern cards have normal+reverse_holo, so this triple-counts each card and is dominated by the priciest run — base1 (Base Set) showed a $28,252 'Full set' value off the 1st-Edition holos despite the user owning a near-complete Unlimited set. The completion % (owned_value_unique / market_value) was correspondingly deflated.
design: DECISION: 'Full set' market value = the minimum cost to own one of every CARD = SUM over cards of MIN(effective price across that card's non-deprecated printings). Collapses to the Unlimited run for WOTC (cheapest of the three) and the base printing for modern sets — the run a set collector actually completes. Chosen over (a) sum-of-all-printings (current, nonsensical) and (b) separate per-print-run totals (more work; user said optional). For base1 this yields ~$1,713 (verified against prod data). owned_value / owned_value_unique unchanged (they reflect real holdings); only the hypothetical full-set figure changes.
acceptance_criteria:
- market_value sums the cheapest printing per card, not all printings.
- Fail-first test: a card with 3 print-run printings (300/800/10000) contributes 300 to market_value, not 11100.
- Existing single-printing-per-card test still asserts 6.0.
- base1 /stats 'Full set' shows ~$1.7k (Unlimited), completion % rises accordingly.
- clippy + fmt clean.
close_reason: market_value now sums MIN(price) per card across non-deprecated printings instead of all printings. Collapses to the Unlimited run for WOTC / base printing for modern sets. base1 verified ~$1,713 vs the old $28,252. Fail-first test (3-run card → 300 not 11100) + existing single-printing test (6.0) both pass; clippy+fmt clean.

title: TTBB copyright-date reprints skipped → bundle orphan slot + 404
description: The TTBB resolver branch in preload_cross_group_products required no parenthetical (!name.contains('(')), so 'Gengar (2022 Copyright Date)' 066/196 (group 23266) and 'Gengar (2021 Copyright Date)' 057/198 (group 3179) were skipped. The base card (e.g. swsh11-66 Lost Origin) never got a stamp_trick_or_trade printing linked to the product, so the bundle binder fell back to a synthetic bundle-product-<id> slot with empty printings and a 'full card details' link that 404s. Reported on /browse/ttbb-2023?page=2 (Gengar).
design: Relax the TTBB branch guard from !name.contains('(') to trailing_paren_lower(name).is_none_or(|p| p.ends_with("copyright date")). The copyright date is a print-run detail the variant taxonomy doesn't model, so route to the same stamp_trick_or_trade code. Verified neither copyright-dated Gengar has a plain TTBB sibling in its group, so no printing-id collision. Fixing resolution fixes both symptoms — the bundle binder LEFT JOINs printings on product_id, so a real printing resolves the slot to the base card with working variants + link.
acceptance_criteria:
- Fail-first test: 'Gengar (2022 Copyright Date)' 066/196 in group 23266 resolves to swsh11-66-stamp_trick_or_trade.
- After refresh, the Gengar slot on /browse/ttbb-2023 shows the stamp_trick_or_trade variant and 'full card details' links to /card/swsh11/66.
- clippy + fmt clean.
close_reason: Relaxed TTBB branch to accept '(YYYY Copyright Date)' parentheticals → stamp_trick_or_trade. Both Gengar copyright-date products now bridge to their base cards; bundle binder resolves the slot via the printings LEFT JOIN, fixing the orphan slot + 404 link. Fail-first test added; 56 ingest tests pass, clippy+fmt clean.

title: Set-stats page blank for bundles (duplicate {#each} key)
description: The /browse/[set]/stats histogram keyed its {#each} on c.number. Bundles (e.g. ttbb-2024) aggregate cards across multiple sets, so the same card number recurs in copy_counts (e.g. #37 appears as both Rare and Common). Duplicate keys make Svelte throw a runtime error that blanks the entire stats page. The analytics API returns valid data — purely a client render crash. Normal sets have unique numbers so they were unaffected.
design: Key the copy_counts {#each} on the array index instead of c.number. The histogram is rebuilt wholesale per load with no per-item state or transitions, so index keying is safe and collision-proof.
acceptance_criteria:
- /browse/ttbb-2024/stats renders the full stats page (histogram + rarity breakdown + value).
- Normal-set stats pages unchanged.
- svelte-check clean.
close_reason: Keyed copy_counts {#each} on array index instead of c.number; bundle card numbers repeat across source sets and the duplicate key threw a Svelte runtime error that blanked the page. svelte-check + build clean.

title: MCAP set-named Prerelease promos not bridged to base cards
description: SV-era Build & Battle / Prerelease promos are named by their SET in the MCAP group (2374), e.g. 'Duraludon (Surging Sparks)' 129/191 = sv8-129, rather than by a '(Prerelease)' stamp suffix. parse_stamp_tag and variant_from_product_name both miss '(Surging Sparks)', so these produced no printing rows and were unenterable. User owns the Surging Sparks Prerelease Duraludon (TCGplayer product 663168).
design: In preload_cross_group_products, after the existing parser branches, add a branch that recognizes a set-named prerelease promo: the trailing parenthetical must equal a real set name AND the collector /total must equal that set's printed_total. Guarded against retailer-exclusive / holo-treatment parentheticals (which don't name sets) by validating against a (lower(name), printed_total) set built from the sets table. Routes to stamp_prerelease with the set name as the disambiguating keyword (reuses the existing keyword match path).
acceptance_criteria:
- Fail-first test: 'Duraludon (Surging Sparks)' 129/191 in MCAP resolves to sv8-129-stamp_prerelease; a 'Klefki - 130/191 (Toys R Us Promo)' with the same /total does NOT bridge.
- After refresh, /card/sv8/129 lists a Prerelease Stamp printing linked to product 663168.
- clippy + fmt clean.
close_reason: Added set-named-prerelease detection in preload_cross_group_products: trailing parenthetical == real set name AND collector /total == that set's printed_total → stamp_prerelease with set keyword. Guarded against retailer/holo parentheticals via a (lower(name),printed_total) HashSet from the sets table. Fail-first test covers Duraludon (Surging Sparks) bridging + Toys R Us negative case. All 55 ingest tests pass, clippy+fmt clean.

title: Cross-group scan misses SV Prerelease promos + Blister cosmos holos
description: Variant expansion only scans CROSS_GROUP_SOURCE_GROUPS=[2374,1840,3179,23266,23561] to resolve cross-group products back to their base card. Two groups of base-set-numbered promos are never scanned, so they produce NO printing rows and the cards are unenterable: (1) group 22872 'SV: Scarlet & Violet Promo Cards' (svp) — Prerelease and Prerelease[Staff] promos carry the base set's collector number (e.g. 'Sinistcha - 022/167 (Prerelease)' = sv6-22) and should bridge as stamp_prerelease / stamp_prerelease_staff; (2) group 2289 'Blister Exclusives' — 130 Cosmos Holo promos numbered against their base set (e.g. 'Beheeyem - 62/99 (Cosmos Holo)') should bridge as cosmos_holo. User owns the Twilight Masquerade Prerelease Sinistcha (TCGplayer product 553715) and could not find/enter it.
design: Add 22872 and 2289 to CROSS_GROUP_SOURCE_GROUPS in crates/pkdump-ingest/src/overrides.rs. The existing matcher is conservative and self-limiting: keyword-less stamps + patterns only bridge when product card_name == base card_name AND product set_total == base printed_total. Bare-numbered svp promos (e.g. 'Aegislash - 060', SVP namespace, no /total) yield set_total=None and therefore never bridge — they remain svp cards. normalize_collector_number('022/167')=='22' so the per-card map lookup hits sv6-22. No schema change; stamp_prerelease/stamp_prerelease_staff/cosmos_holo variant codes already seeded.
acceptance_criteria:
- Fail-first test: a product 'Sinistcha - 022/167 (Prerelease)' in group 22872 resolves to a sv6-22-stamp_prerelease printing during expand_all_printings.
- After refresh on prod, /card/sv6/22 lists a Prerelease Stamp printing linked to product 553715, addable via the normal flow.
- Bare-SVP-numbered promos (e.g. Aegislash 060) are NOT bridged to base sets — regression check that svp cards are unaffected.
- cargo clippy + fmt clean.

title: Display condition-adjusted price per owned copy
description: The /collection table and card-detail 'Your copies' table show market_price as the raw NM market value regardless of the copy's condition. A MP Charizard appears at the full NM market — misleading the user about the copy's true value. Per-printing prices (binder modal, card-detail printings list) stay at NM since those don't have a condition.
design: Add conditionMultiplier() helper to $lib/conditions.ts alongside CONDITIONS. /collection: when aggregating, scale market_unit/market_total by the row's condition multiplier; totalValue rollup uses the same. Card detail 'Your copies' table: replace the 'Paid' column with two columns 'Paid / Value' (or add a Value column) showing the condition-adjusted market price per copy.

- /collection table 'Value' cells reflect NM × cond_mult for the row's condition; a MP Charizard at NM $572 shows $372 (or whatever the comp adjustment yields).
- /collection rollup total at top equals the sum of the displayed adjusted values, not raw NM.
- /card/[set]/[number] 'Your copies' table shows a per-copy estimated value column that respects condition.
- Binder modal printing prices unchanged (per-printing, no copy/condition context).
close_reason: Done. Shared conditionMultiplier() helper in $lib/conditions.ts; /collection per-row Value cells + header total now scale market_price by the row's condition; CardDetailView gains a Value column on the owned-copies table doing the same. Binder modal printing prices unchanged (per-printing, no copy/condition).

title: Group /browse sets by series with collapsible sections + sidebar nav
description: Current /browse renders a flat 175-tile grid. SetSummary.series already gives a 17-bucket taxonomy (Base/Gym/Neo/E-Card/EX/POP/DP/Platinum/HGSS/BW/XY/SM/SwSh/SV/Mega/NP/Other). Make navigation tractable: group tiles by series, collapse by default, expand series where the user owns any cards. Add a sticky sidebar with series quick-links that scroll-and-expand on click and indicate which series have owned cards.
design: Pure frontend refactor of /browse/+page.svelte. Client-side groupBy on SetSummary[].series after fetch. Each series header shows name, set count, aggregate owned/total cards; clickable to toggle collapsed state held in a Record<series, boolean> $state. Default: section is open iff any set in series has owned_cards > 0. Bundles stays a fixed top section. Sidebar (sticky on desktop, horizontal chip row on mobile) lists all series in the same chronological order as the main grid; click jumps to the anchor + force-opens that section. Search input filters tiles within sections; sections with no matches hide. Sort series chronologically newest-first to match the existing release_date DESC ordering.

- /browse renders sets grouped by series under collapsible headers; Bundles stays at the top.
- Series where any contained set has owned_cards > 0 are open by default; the rest are collapsed.
- Sidebar lists every series with a small indicator (e.g. dot or bold) on the ones with owned cards; click scrolls to that anchor and expands the section.
- Search input still works — tiles filter in-place, empty sections hide.
- No backend changes.
close_reason: Done. /browse now groups sets into collapsible series sections; series with any owned cards open by default, others collapse. Sticky sidebar (horizontal chips on mobile) lists every series with a green dot on owned ones; click jumps + auto-expands. Expand-all / Collapse-all buttons. title: Set + edit condition from card modal and card detail
description: Backend already supports condition (CHECK-constrained collection column, PUT /api/collection/{id} with CopyEdit). Frontend only sets it via /ingest/manual today; never lets the user pick at binder-modal add time, never lets the user fix a logged-as-NM copy. Add: (1) condition picker on the VariantModal that defaults to Near Mint and persists at page level for the /browse/[set] session, so both modal + and pip + adds get the chosen condition; (2) inline editable condition cell on CardDetailView's owned-copies table, calling PUT /api/collection/{id}.
design: Extract the five-tier conditions list to $lib/conditions.ts (currently duplicated in /ingest/manual). VariantModal grows a 'condition' prop (bindable) so the parent page owns the value. browse/[set]/+page.svelte holds a $state condition picker, defaulting to Near Mint; sticky across modal opens within the page visit; passed to api.addCopy on both addCopy (modal +) and addToSlot (pip +). CardDetailView replaces the read-only condition <td> with a <select> bound to the row's condition; on change, calls a new api.updateCopy(id, {condition}); optimistic update with revert on error.

- VariantModal shows a Condition <select> at the top with the five tiers; defaults to Near Mint.
- Adding via the modal +, or via the pip + outside the modal, uses the current Condition value.
- Picker stays at the chosen value across modal opens within /browse/[set]; resets to Near Mint when the page is reloaded.
- /card/[set]/[number] table renders each copy's condition as an inline <select>; changing it persists via PUT /api/collection/{id} and the new value sticks after refresh.
- /collection view UNCHANGED (no edit there).

VariantModal grew a bindable condition prop with a <select> picker between header and printings list; defaults to Near Mint, sticky across modal opens. /browse/[set] holds the page-level condition $state and threads it into api.addCopy for both modal + and inline pip +. CardDetailView's Condition cell became an inline <select> that calls a new api.updateCopy(id, {condition}) -> PUT /api/collection/{id}. /collection view unchanged per request.

title: Remove migration versioning; single schema.sql per DB
description: Single-instance project (one user, one prod box). Refinery migrations + V1..V9 history are dead weight. Collapse to one schema file per database using CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, run on every open. Drop refinery dependency, drop the migrations/ directory, drop the migrations module. The existing prod DB is already at V9 — IF NOT EXISTS makes the new init a no-op there. Future schema changes: edit the schema file + manually apply the diff to prod (one box, one user).
design:
1. Use prod DB's .schema output as ground truth for the consolidated schema (validates against the cumulative effect of V1..V9).
2. crates/pkdump-db/src/schema_shared.sql + schema_user.sql, included via include_str!.
3. open_shared and connect_user call conn.execute_batch(SCHEMA_SHARED|USER) instead of refinery.
4. Drop refinery from Cargo.toml workspace + crate, drop migrations.rs module, drop migrations/ directories, drop Migration variant from DbError.
5. fixture.rs: drop the 'clean rebuild' comment about refinery.
6. Existing prod DB keeps its refinery_schema_history table (harmless, not consulted).
acceptance_criteria:
- cargo build clean, cargo clippy clean, cargo test passes (every test that uses open_shared / connect_user works against a fresh DB).
- /api/sets, /api/sets/{code}/binder, /api/sets/{code}/analytics still answer on prod after redeploy.
- Production DB is unchanged in shape (the new init is a no-op there).
- refinery is no longer in Cargo.lock.
close_reason: Refactored: shared and user schemas live in crates/pkdump-db/src/schema_{shared,user}.sql as CREATE … IF NOT EXISTS. open_shared also reconciles variants/sub_type_map/bundles from data/*.json so a freshly-opened shared DB is immediately FK-ready. refinery dropped from workspace + crate, migrations/ directory + migrations.rs gone, DbError::Migration gone. Verified byte-identical schema on a prod-shared/collection copy after running the new init path.

title: Unify bundle UX into set 'container' model
description: Bundle detail page and /browse listing currently diverge sharply from the standard set UX: different tile sizes, different framing, no stats header (base/master progress bars), no view toggle, no sort/search/missing-only controls, no /stats sub-page. Bundles are also missing a /api/sets/{code}/analytics route. User wants a common 'container' abstraction so both sets and bundles render through the same UX, defined at the container level. Also flagged the BUNDLES Rust constant in crates/pkdump-db/src/bundles.rs as a data-model-is-the-product smell — move to data/bundles.json + a bundles table.
design:
Phase 1 (data model): migration V9 adds bundles(slug PK, name, year, tcgcsv_group_id) to shared schema; data/bundles.json seeds it at pkdump setup time; pkdump-db reads from the table; the Rust BUNDLES constant goes away.

Phase 2 (backend unification): SetSummary and BinderSetInfo grow kind: 'set' | 'bundle'. BinderSlot gains optional external_set: { set_code, name } for slots whose underlying card lives in another set (always None for sets, populated for bundles). /api/sets/{code}/binder dispatches to a bundle binder query when {code} is a bundle slug; bundle slots are projected as BinderSlot with section='base', exactly one printing (the TTBB-bridged variant) or zero printings for unresolved slots. Bundle binder query supports the same BinderQuery knobs as sets where they apply (page, layout, sort, q, filter); the section toggles (secret/subset/promos) degrade to no-ops since bundles have a single section. Bundle base_total/master_total both equal slot_count; base_owned/master_owned equal owned-slot count. list_sets returns sets + bundles in one list; bundles surface a synthetic series label ('Trick or Trade Bundle YYYY') and null base_total_cards so the bar gracefully hides.

Phase 3 (frontend): /browse/+page.svelte renders bundles in their own section above sets but using the same .tile shape (logo placeholder, name, series, master progress). /browse/[code]/+page.svelte already handles BinderPage — adds rendering of slot.external_set in card view (a small set-name link under the card name) and a graceful hide of section-toggle controls when set.kind='bundle'. /bundles/[slug]/+page.svelte becomes a redirect to /browse/[slug]; api.bundle/api.bundles can be retired once the frontend stops calling them.

Phase 4 (stats): /api/sets/{code}/analytics also dispatches by slug. Bundle analytics returns degraded shape — base_total/master_total = slot_count; copy_counts/owned_copies from bridged printings; market values from tcgplayer_market_price; rarities optional (skip initially, file follow-up if useful).
acceptance_criteria:
- /browse renders bundle tiles with the same .tile shape as sets (symbol position, progress bar, series line).
- /browse/ttbb-2024 (and the other two TTBB slugs) renders with the same header (base/master progress bars + 'Set stats →' link), same controls row (sort, view toggle, columns stepper, search, missing-only), same binder grid + paging.
- /browse/ttbb-2024/stats loads without 404 and shows at least slot-count completion, copy-count histogram, and total/owned value.
- /bundles/ttbb-2024 still works (redirects to /browse/ttbb-2024) so existing links don't 404.
- BUNDLES is no longer a Rust constant; data/bundles.json + bundles table are the source of truth; reseeding via pkdump setup populates them.
- Bundle slot in 'card view' shows a small link to the underlying card's home set (e.g. 'Obsidian Flames' for the Umbreon TTBB24 slot).
close_reason: Implemented: bundles seeded from data/bundles.json into V9 bundles table; SetSummary/BinderSetInfo gain kind discriminator; BinderSlot gains optional external_set; bundles project to BinderPage and SetAnalytics via dispatch in /api/sets/{code}/binder|analytics. /browse renders bundles in a dedicated section using the same .tile shape. /bundles/[slug] redirects to /browse/[slug]. VariantModal routes the card-detail link via slot.external_set?.set_code. After deploy the user must run pkdump data refresh (or seed.sh prod) to populate the new bundles table.

title: Missing-variant escape hatch on card detail
description: Implement the user_printings escape hatch per decision pokedumpster-x7k. Modal on CardDetailView (and therefore CardModal) lets the user add a copy of any card with an off-catalog variant: free-text description, optional price, qty, note. Visible on /card and CardModal; NOT shown on the binder browse VariantModal.
design:
WORK BREAKDOWN:

1. Add 'missing_variant' to data/variants.json (canonical entry, neutral gray, rank 999, short 'MISS', label 'Missing Variant', provenance describes it as a user-curated catch-all).

2. Shared migration V8: INSERT OR IGNORE the missing_variant row into shared.variants so existing installs pick it up without a full re-setup.

3. User migration V3: CREATE TABLE user_printings (printing_id PK, card_id NOT NULL, variant NOT NULL DEFAULT 'missing_variant', description TEXT, created_at).

4. New crates/pkdump-db/src/user_printings.rs:
   - create(conn, card_id, description, qty, price?, observed_at?, note?) -> i64 (the new collection batch_id? or printing_id)
   - Actually keep it surgical: insert_user_printing(conn, card_id, description) -> String (the new printing_id). The transactional 'add N copies and a manual price' wrapper lives in the route handler, since it composes existing functions.
   - delete(conn, printing_id) — returns whether deleted; refuses if collection rows reference it.
   - exists(conn, printing_id) — used by manual_prices::insert FK check.
   - Tests inline.

5. Update manual_prices::insert FK check to accept either shared.printings or user_printings. Add a fail-first test.

6. Update cards::get_card_detail printings query to UNION ALL shared.printings with user_printings. Add a new field is_user_added: bool and description: Option<String> to PrintingInfo. Add gap-fill (already done) — the COALESCE inside the printing-info query yields NULL for tcg, falls back to manual_prices.

7. cards::get_card_prices: same UNION pattern so the chart endpoint includes user_printings (they'll only have a 'manual' series).

8. New routes/user_printings.rs:
   - POST /api/user-printings  body: {card_id, description, qty, price?, observed_at?, note?}
     Returns {printing_id, copies_added: Vec<CollectionRow>}. Uses an immediate-mode transaction.
   - DELETE /api/user-printings/{printing_id}
   
9. Frontend:
   - Generated PrintingInfo TS picks up is_user_added + description automatically.
   - New MissingVariantModal.svelte: description, price, datetime-local (optional), qty stepper, note.
   - 'Add missing variant' button next to the Printings heading on CardDetailView.
   - Italic + (user) tag rendering on printings rows where is_user_added.

10. Tests:
   - DB unit: create_user_printing produces a printing_id matching '{card_id}-user-{N}', N increments per card.
   - DB unit: get_card_detail returns user_printings alongside shared printings.
   - DB unit: manual_prices::insert accepts a user_printing printing_id.
   - DB unit: get_card_prices includes a 'manual' series for a user_printing with a price.
   - DB unit: binder query DOES NOT include user_printings (existing test still passes; no new test needed).
   - DB unit: delete_user_printing refuses when collection references it.
   - UI scenario: add a missing variant 'no set stamp misprint' to Jungle Jolteon with qty=1 and price=$200; expect to see it on /card with italic label, in the collection page with the right market_price.
acceptance_criteria: (1) Migrations apply cleanly to a copy of the live prod DB. (2) POST /api/user-printings creates user_printing + collection + manual_price atomically. (3) /api/card/jungle/4 returns the new printing as part of the printings list with is_user_added=true. (4) /api/collection shows the new copies with the manual price as market_price. (5) /api/sets/jungle/binder does NOT include user_printings (binder modal stays catalog-only). (6) cargo clippy + fmt clean; all tests pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: Missing-variant escape hatch via user-DB user_printings table
description: Need a way to log copies of cards whose variant isn't in the catalog yet (motivating case: Jungle Jolteon/Pinsir with the missing-set-stamp misprint). Should be available wherever you'd normally add a copy of a known printing, except for the binder browse popup which should only show catalog data.
design:
STORAGE: New table 'user_printings' in the user DB (collection.sqlite), not shared.sqlite. Reason: shared is rebuilt by 'pkdump setup' and would clobber user data. New refinery migration V3 in crates/pkdump-db/migrations/user/.

SCHEMA: user_printings(printing_id PK, card_id TEXT NOT NULL, variant TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'missing_variant', description TEXT, created_at TEXT). printing_id format: '{card_id}-user-{N}' where N is a per-card sequence.

CANONICAL VARIANT: Add 'missing_variant' to data/variants.json and seed it into shared.variants via a new shared migration V8. Label 'Missing Variant', short 'MISS', rank 999 (sorts last), neutral gray color.

EFFECTIVE-PRICE: Reuses manual_prices keyed by printing_id (the gap-fill rule then degenerates to 'manual is the only price' since there's no TCGplayer link). manual_prices::insert FK check accepts either shared.printings or user_printings as the parent.

QUERY CHANGES: get_card_detail UNION ALL's user_printings (with NULL for tcgplayer_product_id, sub_type_name, etc.) so the printings list on /card and CardModal includes them. The binder query in pkdump-db/src/binder.rs is NOT touched — VariantModal stays catalog-only per the user's explicit ask.

UX: Single 'Add missing variant' modal on CardDetailView (used by both /card and CardModal). Form fields: description (optional free text), price (optional), qty (default 1), note. Submit does: (1) create user_printing row, (2) insert qty collection rows pointing at it, (3) optionally insert one manual_prices row.

DISPLAY: Italic label + small 'user' tag on the printings list. Color chip in the printings list only — NO chip on the binder browse view (binder query already won't see these).
acceptance_criteria: (1) Decision recorded; schema + UX unambiguous. (2) Subsequent feature issue can be implemented mechanically.
close_reason: Closed

title: Browse-set tile redesign: 'card view' with per-tile metadata vs binder-view
description:
Today the set browse page (/browse/<set_code>) shows only the card image and variant pips per tile. Add more per-tile metadata (collector number, name, possibly market price / rarity) so the page is useful as a scanning view. Two intended modes:

- BINDER VIEW (current): visually mimics a physical binder page. Image + pips, minimal chrome. Good for at-a-glance recognition.
- CARD VIEW (new): image + collector number + name + maybe market/owned-count. Better for finding a specific card or scanning the set as data.

Default and toggle behaviour TBD — likely a segmented control at the top of /browse/<set_code> with the user's choice persisted in collection.sqlite settings table.
acceptance_criteria: (1) Two visually distinct modes on /browse/<set>. (2) Toggle persists across page reloads. (3) Card view shows at least the collector number; further fields are a follow-up discussion.
close_reason: Closed

title: Manual price entry on card detail
description: Implement manual prices per decision pokedumpster-7bc: a user-DB table 'manual_prices' (printing_id, price, observed_at, note, created_at), with gap-fill semantics — TCGplayer market wins when present, manual fills the gap. Entry UI is a modal on /card/<set>/<number>.
design:
WORK BREAKDOWN:

1. Migration: V2 in crates/pkdump-db/migrations/user/ creates manual_prices table + index on (printing_id, observed_at DESC).

2. Db layer (crates/pkdump-db/src/manual_prices.rs):
   - insert_manual_price(conn, printing_id, price, observed_at: Option<DateTime>, note: Option<String>)
   - list_manual_prices_for_printing(conn, printing_id) -> Vec<ManualPrice>
   - delete_manual_price(conn, id)
   Tests in same file using existing in-memory user-DB harness.

3. Update get_card_prices (crates/pkdump-db/src/cards.rs ~L201): LEFT JOIN manual_prices so the response includes a 'manual' series per printing. Frontend chart can then render both lines. Keep gap-fill specifically for the 'effective current price' computation — keep both visible in the time series chart.

4. API routes (crates/pkdump-server/src/routes/card.rs or a new prices.rs):
   - POST /api/card/<set>/<number>/manual-price  { printing_id, price, observed_at?, note? }
   - DELETE /api/manual-price/<id>
   - GET piggybacks on existing /api/card/<set>/<number>/prices.

5. Frontend (frontend/src/routes/card/[set]/[number]/+page.svelte):
   - 'Add price' button per printing card opens a modal with: price input, datetime-local input (default now), note input.
   - Show history table below price chart.
   - Use existing typed api object in /api.ts.

6. Collection-value queries: anywhere we sum the latest TCGplayer price across owned cards (none today as runtime endpoints but the ad-hoc query I ran earlier), the rule going forward is COALESCE(latest tcg market, latest manual). Document in the manual_prices.rs module docstring.

7. Tests:
   - DB unit: insert + read back; default timestamp is recent; explicit timestamp honored.
   - DB unit: gap-fill correctness — printing with no TCG row falls back to latest manual.
   - DB unit: when both exist, TCG wins for effective price (but both visible in time series).
   - UI scenario: open card detail, click Add price, enter $200 manually on a basep printing, confirm it shows up.
acceptance_criteria: (1) Migration applies cleanly to a fresh user DB. (2) Adding a manual price for one of the 6 basep printings causes /api/card/basep/14/prices to include it. (3) Modal flow works end-to-end on /card/basep/14. (4) Re-running the original 14-set query with the new COALESCE rule shows basep > $0 once a manual price exists. (5) cargo clippy clean, cargo fmt clean, all tests pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: Manual prices: user-DB table keyed by printing_id, gap-fill semantics
description: Need a way to record prices for printings that the TCGplayer feed doesn't cover (basep is the immediate motivating case — 6 owned promos with no tcgplayer_product_id, hence zero contribution to collection-value sums). Want the entries to be timestamped time series, with the timestamp defaulting to now() but overridable so external time series can be backfilled.
design:
STORAGE: New table 'manual_prices' in the user DB (collection.sqlite), not shared.sqlite. Reason: shared is rebuilt by 'pkdump setup' and would clobber user data; user DB survives catalog refreshes. New refinery migration in crates/pkdump-db/migrations/user/.

SCHEMA: manual_prices(id PK, printing_id TEXT NOT NULL, price REAL NOT NULL, observed_at TEXT NOT NULL, note TEXT, created_at TEXT DEFAULT datetime('now')). Keyed by printing_id (not tcgplayer_product_id) so basep cards with no TCG mapping work. App-layer FK to shared.printings (no cross-DB FK).

EFFECTIVE-PRICE RULE: Gap-fill semantics. TCGplayer market price always wins when present; manual_prices is only consulted when no TCGplayer row exists for the printing. Implemented as COALESCE(tcg_market, latest_manual) in the get_card_prices / collection-value queries.

SCOPE: Per printing, not per collection copy. Matches existing prices shape; one time series per (card, variant, sub_type).

UI: Card detail page modal/dialog. CLI not needed in v1.
acceptance_criteria: (1) Decision recorded; schema fields and gap-fill rule unambiguous. (2) Subsequent feature issue can be implemented mechanically from this.
close_reason: Closed

title: Antique Cover Fossil (zsv10pt5-80) misplaced + /card 404 due to upstream number='60'
description:
Reproduction: http://192.168.1.93:8090/browse/zsv10pt5?page=7 shows card "Antique Cover Fossil" with collector number 80 wedged between #60 (Escavalier) and #61 (Klink) on the lower-left of the binder grid. http://192.168.1.93:8090/card/zsv10pt5/80 returns 404 (\`/api/card/zsv10pt5/80\` → HTTP 404). \`/api/card/zsv10pt5/60\` returns Escavalier, masking Antique Cover Fossil entirely.

Root cause (upstream, not us): pokemontcg.io's row for \`zsv10pt5-80\` has \`id: "zsv10pt5-80"\` and image URL \`https://images.pokemontcg.io/zsv10pt5/80.png\` (both correctly say "80") but \`number: "60"\`. Verified live against \`https://api.pokemontcg.io/v2/cards/zsv10pt5-80\` on 2026-05-25 — not a stale cache; a \`pkdump data refresh\` will not help.

Why the symptoms: \`get_card_detail\` in \`crates/pkdump-db/src/cards.rs:130\` looks up cards by \`WHERE set_code = ?1 AND c.number = ?2\`, so any caller passing "80" finds nothing while "60" returns the first matching row (Escavalier).

Scope: this is the ONLY upstream row in the entire shared catalog with this kind of \`card_id\` ↔ \`number\` disagreement. Verified via:
\`\`\`sql
SELECT card_id, set_code, number, substr(card_id, length(set_code) + 2) AS suffix
  FROM cards
 WHERE raw_json IS NOT NULL
   AND substr(card_id, length(set_code) + 2) != number
   AND substr(card_id, length(set_code) + 2) NOT LIKE '%\\_%' ESCAPE '\\';
-- → 1 row: zsv10pt5-80 / 60 / 80
\`\`\`
(The \`cel25c-N_A\` Classic-Collection rows are intentional multi-printing disambiguators and are excluded.)
design:
Two plausible approaches; user to pick.

**A. Explicit override seed file (recommended).** Add \`data/overrides/upstream_card_corrections.json\`, list of \`{ card_id, set?: ..., number?: ..., ... }\` entries. After upstream cards are ingested, a final phase applies the overrides. First entry: \`{ "card_id": "zsv10pt5-80", "number": "80" }\`. Matches the existing pattern of \`data/overrides/variant_augmentations.json\` and CLAUDE.md's "data IS the product" guidance. The override file becomes the registry of known upstream-data corrections — easy to extend.

**B. Card-id suffix heal.** At ingest, when the trailing segment after \`set_code-\` is pure digits and disagrees with upstream \`number\`, overwrite \`number\` to match the id suffix. One-line fix, but introduces an implicit rule. Today this would only affect zsv10pt5-80, but it'd silently auto-correct any future similar upstream rows without leaving a paper trail.

Both: same fail-first test (currently passing) — a row exists for \`zsv10pt5-80\` with \`number = '80'\`, \`get_card_detail("zsv10pt5", "80")\` returns the card, binder query for page 7 places it in slot 80.
acceptance_criteria:
- \`/api/card/zsv10pt5/80\` returns Antique Cover Fossil (not 404).
- \`/browse/zsv10pt5?page=7\` places Antique Cover Fossil in slot 80, not adjacent to Escavalier in slot 60.
- A test reproducing the wrong placement / 404 was added in the same commit as the fix (fail-first).
- No regression in any other set's binder placement.
close_reason: Closed

title: Bridge TTBB groups into variant expansion (cross-group source allowlist)
description:
Extend variant expansion in \`crates/pkdump-ingest/src/overrides.rs\` so Trick or Trade BOOster Bundle products attach as variants of their parent cards.

**Change.** Add the three TTBB TCGplayer group IDs to \`CROSS_GROUP_SOURCE_GROUPS\` (currently \`[2374, 1840]\`). \`preload_cross_group_products\` already keys by normalized collector_number; for every TTBB product whose \`collector_number\` resolves to a base card in another set, expansion will pick it up automatically.

Group IDs:
- 3179  — Trick or Trade BOOster Bundle (2022)
- 23266 — Trick or Trade BOOster Bundle 2023
- 23561 — Trick or Trade BOOster Bundle 2024

**Variant codes.** Whatever pokedumpster-vz2 concludes — at minimum \`cosmos_holo\` for the 10 TTBB24 products that already carry \`derived_variant = 'cosmos_holo'\`. Additional codes may be needed for 2022/2023/2024 plain reprints depending on the research.

**Resolution path.** TTBB products come in two name shapes that need to dispatch differently:
1. \`"Darkrai (Cosmos Holo) 136/197"\` — parenthetical pattern, \`derived_variant\` already populated by tcgcsv ingest. Existing pattern-overlay resolution in \`preload_cross_group_products\` handles these.
2. \`"Phantump 016/196"\` — bare name (no parenthetical). Today this shape only resolves via the Deck Exclusives path (\`DECK_EXCLUSIVES_GROUP_ID\`), which uses \`prices.sub_type_name\` to pick a variant. TTBB doesn't fit that model. Likely needs a new resolution branch: "bare-name product in a TTBB group → attach with the year-specific variant code". Implement that branch only for years where vz2 says a distinct variant is needed.

**Test.** Add fail-first integration tests modeled on \`cross_group_cosmos_holo_attaches_to_numbered_set_card\` and \`cross_group_deck_exclusive_non_foil_attaches_to_base_card\`:
- One for a TTBB24 Cosmos Holo product attaching to its parent.
- One per year where a new variant code is introduced.

**Re-ingest.** After landing, run \`pkdump data refresh\` (or \`deploy/seed.sh prod\` if local catalog is stale) so existing TTBB products become printings.
acceptance_criteria:
- \`CROSS_GROUP_SOURCE_GROUPS\` includes 3179, 23266, 23561.
- TTBB24 Cosmos Holo products show up as variants on their parent card pages.
- All TTBB products that ought to attach (per vz2 disposition) have at least one matching \`printings\` row.
- Fail-first integration tests demonstrate at least the Cosmos Holo path and any new variant code paths.
- No regressions in existing MCAP/Deck-Exclusives expansion tests.
close_reason: Closed

title: Research TTBB variant codes (2022/2023/2024) before ingest bridge lands
description:
Blocking the TTBB ingest extension. Before we add the three TTBB groups to \`CROSS_GROUP_SOURCE_GROUPS\` we need to know what variant code each TTBB product should attach as, because that determines whether they become duplicates of the parent printing or a distinct variant chip.

Open TCGplayer (or images.pokemontcg.io if it has them) and inspect sample products from each group:

- **TTBB 2022 (group 3179, 30 products, all \`derived_variant IS NULL\`):** Sample products: 283766 "Gengar (2021 Copyright Date) 057/198", 283785 "Mewtwo 056/172", 283790 "Chandelure 033/192". Question: do these carry a 2022 Halloween jack-o'-lantern stamp/marking, or are they bare reprints visually identical to the parent set's non-foil? If stamped → new variant code (proposal: \`ttbb_2022\`, label "Trick or Trade 2022", short tag "TTBB22"). If identical → don't bridge these products at all (they'd just duplicate the parent printing).
- **TTBB 2023 (group 23266, 30 products, all \`derived_variant IS NULL\`):** Sample products: 515647 "Phantump 016/196", 515654 "Pikachu 062/193", 515661 "Gengar (2022 Copyright Date) 066/196". Same question for 2023.
- **TTBB 2024 (group 23561, mix):** 10 products tagged \`cosmos_holo\` (already a known variant). 20 products with no derived_variant. Cosmos Holo: should just work once the group is bridged. Plain products: same question — stamped/distinct or bare reprint?

For any year where a new variant code is needed, add a row to \`data/variants.json\` (label, short tag, sort rank, chip color). For Halloween stamps, propose chip color in the orange/purple family.

Note: \`cosmos_holo\` already exists in \`data/variants.json\` and the tcgcsv ingest already parses it for TTBB24 products. Confirm but no schema work needed there.

Output of this task: an answer per year (bridge-as-variant with code X / bridge-as-duplicate-skip / don't bridge) recorded as notes on the parent decision pokedumpster-gnh.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each of the three TTBB years has a documented disposition: variant code + label, or "skip" with reason.
- \`data/variants.json\` updated for any newly-needed codes.
- pokedumpster-gnh updated with the conclusion (--notes).
notes:
Research outcome (2026-05-26): all three TTBB years use the same Halloween Pikachu jack-o-lantern stamp on the card artwork — confirmed by inspecting sample TCGplayer product images vs the parent set images for 2022 (Chandelure 033/192 vs Rebel Clash), 2023 (Chandelure 026/196 vs Lost Origin), and 2024 (Umbreon 130/197 vs Obsidian Flames). All TTBB versions carry the stamp; parents have none.

The 10 TTBB 2024 Cosmos Holo cards carry the stamp PLUS a Cosmos Holo background treatment; the Cosmos Holo treatment is TTBB-2024-exclusive (modern sets don't otherwise ship Cosmos Holo).

Decision (owner: ryan): use TWO new variant codes.
- `stamp_trick_or_trade` — for all 60 plain-name TTBB reprints across 2022, 2023, and 2024.
- `cosmos_holo_trick_or_trade` — for the 10 TTBB 2024 Cosmos Holo specials; combined code keeps the TTBB exclusivity explicit on the variant chip.

Added both to `data/variants.json` (label, short=TOT, color=Halloween orange #e7732f / #e88a3a).

Note for bn9: tcgcsv parser today emits `derived_variant = 'cosmos_holo'` for the 10 Cosmos products (matches the "(Cosmos Holo)" parenthetical). bn9 must remap that to `cosmos_holo_trick_or_trade` when the product lives in group 23561, OR the parser needs a TTBB-aware branch. Recommend: do the remap inside the cross-group bridge in `expand_all_printings` rather than complicating the generic parser, since group 23561 is the only place this combination occurs.
close_reason: Decision recorded; variants.json updated. Next: pokedumpster-bn9 picks up the ingest bridge.

title: How to surface Trick or Trade BOOster Bundle (TTBB) cards
description:
TCGCSV exposes three Trick or Trade BOOster Bundle groups — TTBB (group 3179, 2022, 30 products), TTBB23 (23266, 2023, 30 products), TTBB24 (23561, 2024, 30 products). pokemontcg.io has no matching set rows for any of them, and none of our \`sets\` map their \`tcgcsv_group_id\` at them. As a result the /browse page never lists them, and zero \`printings\` reference any TTBB product ID — even though each TTBB product carries a collector_number that resolves to a real card in another set.

User decision (2026-05-25, owner: ryan): **variants-primary**, with a secondary logical-set entry-path view.

Rationale: every TTBB product is numbered for a card that exists in some other set (e.g. TTBB23 "Phantump 016/196" → Lost Origin 016; TTBB24 "Darkrai (Cosmos Holo) 136/197" → Paldea Evolved 136). The physical card is the same Pokémon at the same collector number — sometimes with a TTBB-exclusive finish (Cosmos Holo in 2024) or a Halloween stamp (need to verify 2022/2023). So the canonical model is: extend variant expansion to attach TTBB products to their parent cards, with appropriate variant codes. A logical-set view is added on top purely as a data-entry affordance so the user can input a whole TTBB pack from one page instead of navigating to 30 individual cards.
design:
**Variant attachment.** Extend the cross-group bridge in \`crates/pkdump-ingest/src/overrides.rs\` (\`CROSS_GROUP_SOURCE_GROUPS\`, currently \`[2374, 1840]\`) to also include the three TTBB group IDs: \`3179, 23266, 23561\`. \`preload_cross_group_products\` already keys by normalized collector_number, so resolution falls out for free once the groups are in the allowlist — every TTBB product whose \`collector_number\` matches a card in a real pokemontcg.io set will be picked up and become a printing of that card.

**Variant codes (needs research before code):**
- TTBB 2024 Cosmos Holo: \`derived_variant = 'cosmos_holo'\` is already populated for these by tcgcsv ingest. The \`cosmos_holo\` variant code already exists in data/variants.json. Should just work.
- TTBB 2024 plain (no parenthetical, e.g. "Sprigatito - 012/193"): need to confirm whether these are visually identical to the parent set printing or carry a TTBB-exclusive marking (Halloween stamp etc.). If identical → don't attach (it's a duplicate of the parent). If distinct → introduce a \`ttbb_2024\` or similar variant code.
- TTBB 2023 plain reprints (group 23266, all 30 products have \`derived_variant IS NULL\`): same question — confirm whether they carry a 2023 Halloween stamp or are bare reprints. Likely need a \`ttbb_2023\` variant code with a Halloween stamp label.
- TTBB 2022 plain reprints (group 3179, mostly bare-name): same — likely \`ttbb_2022\` with a stamp label.

Open the TCGplayer product pages for a few sample products from each group; check the card image for distinguishing marks before deciding.

**Logical-set view (secondary).** Do NOT seed real rows in the \`sets\` table for TTBB. Instead add a /ttbb (or /sets/ttbb) route that, given a TTBB group_id, lists the 30 products in collector_number order and renders each as a slot linking to the *parent card's* binder slot (with the TTBB variant preselected for the +1 affordance). This keeps the data model honest: TTBB has no set in pokemontcg.io, so it shouldn't synthesize one. The view is pure UI sugar over \`tcgcsv_products\` joined to \`printings\` via product_id.

The /browse page should still surface this view via a tile or sidebar entry ("Trick or Trade Bundles") so the user can find it.
acceptance_criteria:
- Decision recorded: variants-primary, with logical-set entry view as secondary affordance.
- TTBB variant-code question is researched (parent-identical vs. distinct stamp/finish) per year before any ingest code lands.
- Follow-up feature issue(s) created for: (1) extend cross-group bridge to TTBB groups + add any new variant codes; (2) logical-set entry view; (3) /browse surface for the entry view.
notes: TTBB variant codes settled in pokedumpster-vz2: stamp_trick_or_trade (60 plain reprints) + cosmos_holo_trick_or_trade (10 TTBB 2024 Cosmos specials). Both added to data/variants.json. bn9 (ingest bridge) unblocked.

title: Normalize set symbol glyphs at ingest time
description:
Upstream pokemontcg.io symbol PNGs are not uniformly sized — PNG canvases range from 25x15 (POR/me2) to 38x38 (TWM/sv6) and contain varying amounts of transparent padding. The browse/+page.svelte tile uses height: 28px with width auto, so the rendered glyph size varies wildly across sets. Toggling to height: auto is worse.

Fix at the data layer: during catalog ingest, fetch each set's upstream symbol PNG, trim the alpha bbox, resize to a uniform target height (64px = 2x the 28px CSS size for retina crispness), and self-host under $PKDUMP_HOME/symbols/<set_code>.png. Rewrite sets.symbol_url to /sym/<set_code>.png. Add a new column symbol_source_url so 'pkdump data refresh' can detect when pokemontcg.io rotates a symbol and re-trim.

Server gains nest_service('/sym', ServeDir::new(data_dir.join('symbols'))) — analogous to the existing /sets route but data-volume-backed instead of image-baked. Override symbol_urls (/sets/mep-symbol.svg etc.) are left untouched: bridge file still wins.
design: Schema V3: ALTER TABLE sets ADD COLUMN symbol_source_url TEXT. Ingest module pkdump-ingest/src/symbols.rs::normalize_all_symbols(conn, data_dir). Idempotent: skips when symbol_source_url matches and the file exists. Fetch/decode errors log + skip + leave the row's URL untouched (best-effort enrichment, must not fail catalog refresh). Uses the 'image' crate for PNG decode/encode + Lanczos3 resize.
acceptance_criteria: 1) After pkdump setup, every set with an http(s) symbol_url has a corresponding file at $PKDUMP_HOME/symbols/<set_code>.png. 2) sets.symbol_url for those sets points at /sym/<set_code>.png. 3) Override symbol_urls (those starting with /) are untouched. 4) GET /sym/sv6.png returns the trimmed-and-normalized PNG. 5) On the /browse page, all set glyphs visibly render at the same height with no padding variance. 6) pkdump data refresh re-trims only when the upstream symbol_url has changed (symbol_source_url comparison).

title: MEP (Mega Evolution Promo) absent from /browse — synthesize sets rows for orphan TCGCSV promo groups
description:
TCGCSV has group 24451 'ME: Mega Evolution Promo' (abbreviation MEP, 83 products, published 2025-09-26), but our 'sets' table has no row for it. So MEP never appears in the browse selection, even though we already have the catalog data and pricing.

This is the same shape as SVP (TCGCSV group 22872 'SV: Scarlet & Violet Promo Cards'). SVP shows up in /browse only because pokemontcg.io has a 'svp' set entry (ptcgo_code PR-SV) — even with sets.tcgcsv_group_id NULL, the set still renders. MEP has no pokemontcg.io counterpart, so it has no sets row at all.

Two separate gaps revealed here:
1. pokemontcg.io has not published a 'Mega Evolution Promo' set (~8 months past release — beyond the usual 2–3 month upstream lag).
2. Our linker resolve_group_set_links in crates/pkdump-ingest/src/tcgcsv.rs:240-258 matches by ptcgo_code abbreviation then normalized set name. Even if pokemontcg.io adds MEP, the abbreviations almost certainly won't match (TCGCSV uses 'MEP', pokemontcg.io will likely use 'PR-ME' following the PR-SV / PR-SW / PR-SM pattern), and the normalized names won't match either ('SV: Scarlet & Violet Promo Cards' vs 'Scarlet & Violet Black Star Promos' is the existing precedent). So the auto-linker won't bridge MEP automatically once upstream catches up.
design:
Two options to evaluate:

Option A (lightweight, immediate): hand-bridge in an overrides file. Add data/overrides/tcgcsv_set_bridges.json mapping {tcgcsv_group_id -> set_code} OR {tcgcsv_abbreviation -> ptcgo_code}. The linker reads this overlay last, after the abbreviation+name auto-match. This also fixes SVP at the same time.

Option B (more general): synthesize a sets row for any TCGCSV group that survives the auto-link pass without a match and looks like a 'promo set' (abbreviation ends in 'P', or has 'Promo' in name, or 'Black Star' in name). Synthetic sets get a generated set_code (e.g. 'mep'), the TCGCSV group's name and published_on, and tcgcsv_group_id wired up. Risk: synthesizing creates rows that pokemontcg.io will eventually duplicate, leaving us with split data.

Recommend Option A: an explicit overlay is the canonical 'manual bridge' for ingest gaps in this codebase (see variant_augmentations.json — same pattern). Per CLAUDE.md, data, not logic.
acceptance_criteria:
- After running pkdump setup / data refresh: sets table has a row joined to TCGCSV group 24451 (MEP). Cards from MEP appear in browse.
- SVP gets a real tcgcsv_group_id link via the same mechanism (currently NULL despite having a sets row).
- Overrides file is small, readable, hand-maintained.
notes: Investigation context: PFL Zacian issue conversation. SVP currently has set_code='svp', ptcgo_code='PR-SV', tcgcsv_group_id=NULL — the auto-linker did not bridge it to TCGCSV group 22872. That's a pre-existing data integrity gap this issue would also close.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 639a5b1 — added data/overrides/tcgcsv_set_bridges.json with SVP link + MEP synthesize entries. Verified against prod DB copy: svp now points to TCGCSV group 22872, mep set row created with group 24451. Follow-up pokedumpster-itw covers card-row synthesis for the empty MEP tile.

title: Variant expansion ignores TCGCSV group 1840 'Deck Exclusives' — drops non-foil deck-origin rares
description:
The variant expander in crates/pkdump-ingest/src/overrides.rs scans only the card's own TCGCSV group plus one cross-group catch-all, hard-coded as MISC_GROUP_ID = 2374 (MCAP).

It does NOT scan group 1840 ('Deck Exclusives'), which is the canonical TCGCSV home for non-foil cards that ship inside preconstructed products (Build & Battle decks, theme decks, Battle Academies, etc.). Group 1840 currently holds 479 products spanning XY-era through current; 331 of them have a 'Normal' sub_type price entry. Every one of those is a real non-foil printing that PokeDumpster is silently dropping.

Concrete repro: I have a non-foil rare Zacian 045/094 from Phantasmal Flames (me2-45). TCGCSV product 664005 lives in group 1840 with sub_type 'Normal'. PokeDumpster has only me2-45-holo and me2-45-reverse_holo printings — no normal variant. The me2-45-normal printing should exist.
design:
Per CLAUDE.md 'data model is the product': the set of cross-group source groups should be data, not a Rust constant.

Two-step fix:

1. Replace MISC_GROUP_ID constant with a list of cross-group source group IDs. Could be a small static array in code for now; eventually a seed file alongside variants.json.

2. Extend preload_cross_group_products to scan group 1840 as well. Modern bare-name products in 1840 (e.g. 'Cinderace - 028/198', 'Zacian - 045/094') have no parenthetical pattern — they need a new resolution branch that defaults their sub_type-derived variant to 'normal' via sub_type_to_variant. Older 1840 products with parentheticals like (Cracked Ice Holo) / (XY Base Set) already route through variant_from_product_name.

Match logic for 1840 is the same as non-stamp MCAP overlays: collector_number normalize-match, plus card_name_lower + set_total disambiguation when set_keyword is absent (it always will be for plain 1840 entries).
acceptance_criteria:
- Fail-first test: card me2-45 with TCGCSV product 664005 in group 1840 (sub_type 'Normal') produces a me2-45-normal printing after expand_all_printings runs.
- Existing tests for group 2374 (MCAP) behavior still pass.
- After running 'pkdump data refresh' against a real catalog: me2-45-normal exists in printings; spot-check a handful of other modern bare-name 1840 entries (e.g. Cinderace - 028/198) also get normal printings on their base cards.
- No regressions on patterned 1840 products like Yveltal - 78/146 (Cracked Ice Holo) — those continue to resolve via the existing pattern parser.
notes: Investigation context: see conversation that produced this issue. The 331 'Normal' sub_type count in group 1840 is the upper bound on the number of new printings this will create across the whole catalog; the actual write count will be lower because some collector numbers won't have a matching pokemontcg.io card.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 678e487 — cross-group preload now scans group 1840 in addition to 2374, and uses sub_type_to_variant for bare-name products. Fail-first test covers Zacian PFL case + leak guard.

description:

Acceptance:

- Specify how it maps onto each surface (in-set narrowing vs full-catalog).

title: pkdump setup — variant expansion rate drops 3x past ~9000 cards
description: Live progress instrumentation revealed expand_all_printings throughput collapses from ~150 cards/s to ~55 cards/s once it gets past ~card 9000, and keeps degrading. The shared catalog connection only sets PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON — no WAL, no cache_size bump, no synchronous tuning. With the default ~2MB page cache, once the printings table + its indices exceed cache size every per-card UPDATE/INSERT round-trips to disk; default fsync-on-commit also serializes every per-card transaction. Fix: in open_shared(), set PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL + synchronous=NORMAL + cache_size=-65536 (64MB). Expected: cliff disappears, total expansion drops from ~370s to well under 100s.
close_reason: open_shared() now sets PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL, synchronous=NORMAL, cache_size=-65536 (64MB) — WAL keeps writes sequential, NORMAL drops the per-commit fsync (crash-safe in WAL), 64MB cache keeps the printings table + indices hot through the entire per-card transaction loop.

Add a small sort bar above the grid that drives the shared sortKey/sortDir state, and have the grid iterate over a per-copy sortedRows derived list.

title: variants::reconcile doesn't refresh migration-backfilled raw-code labels
description: V2 migration backfills any non-seed printings.variant code into variants with the raw code as label (so the FK rebuild can finish). reconcile() then only synthesizes for rows MISSING from variants — but the migration row already exists. Net effect: dynamic stamp variants (e.g. stamp_prismatic_evolutions) display the raw code in the UI instead of 'Prismatic Evolutions Stamp'. Found in prod after seed run.
