title: Attach MCAP non-stamp products (Cosmo Holo, etc.) to numbered-set base cards
description:
preload_stamp_products in crates/pkdump-ingest/src/overrides.rs only matches MCAP (group 2374) products whose name parses as a stamp tag. Other treatments MCAP hosts — currently observed: Cosmo Holo — are silently dropped, so cards like Erika's Tangela in ME2.5 (#7, MCAP product 679253 'Erika's Tangela 007/217 Cosmo Holo') are missing their fourth variant.

Generalise the cross-group attach: parse the parenthetical via parse_product_card_name + variant_from_product_name (plus new 'cosmo holo' / 'cosmos holo' matcher), resolve to a base card by collector number + set-name-keyword / printed_total the same way stamps already do, and emit the printing with the appropriate variant code. The variants table already knows cosmos_holo; this is the ingest side.
close_reason: Implemented at ingest time: variant_from_product_name now recognizes 'cosmo holo' / 'cosmos holo' / 'cosmos holofoil' → cosmos_holo. preload_stamp_products generalized into preload_cross_group_products which tries the stamp parser then falls back to the pattern parser, so any MCAP non-stamp overlay attaches to its base card the same way stamps do. Integration test added (cross_group_cosmos_holo_attaches_to_numbered_set_card).

title: Move variant display metadata into a shared.sqlite `variants` table
description: Variant display data (label, sort rank, chip color, short table tag) currently lives in four scattered TS/Svelte functions plus a Rust KNOWN_VARIANTS constant. Move all of it into a single shared.sqlite table seeded from data/variants.json at `pkdump setup` time. Add a FK from printings.variant so ingest can no longer silently introduce unknown codes.
design:
Schema:
- variants(code PK, label, short, rank, color) — all NOT NULL
- printings.variant becomes FK -> variants(code)

Source of truth: data/variants.json (flat list of {code,label,short,rank,color} records). pkdump setup re-seeds the table (DELETE + INSERT) so the file is authoritative.

API: GET /api/variants returns the full list. Frontend fetches once on first need and caches in a /variants.svelte.ts store; the four display functions collapse to map lookups.

Migrations:
- shared migration N: CREATE TABLE variants ... + seed (initial rows so the FK can be added)
- shared migration N+1: ALTER printings ADD constraint (or rebuild via temp table — SQLite has no direct ADD FK).

Removes the 'Rh → Reverse Holo' stopgap in variantLabel() since the label is now data.
close_reason: Implemented: V2 migration adds variants(code,label,short,rank,color) with FK from printings.variant; data/variants.json is the canonical seed; pkdump_db::variants::{reconcile,ensure_code,list_all} drive setup/ingest; /api/variants endpoint feeds a Svelte 5 $state store that replaces the four scattered TS heuristics (variantLabel/Rank/Color/Tag).

title: Pattern variants for ASC/BLK/WHT: codes, linker auto-create, sub_type pricing

TCGCSV publishes per-pattern card products for these sets but our catalog has no overlay rules and no variant codes for the new patterns. Audit found:

- BLK + WHT: Poke Ball Pattern (80 cards each), Master Ball Pattern (72 cards each)
- ASC: Energy Symbol Pattern (140), Poke Ball (34), Dusk Ball (26), Love Ball (25), Friend Ball (23), Quick Ball (22), Team Rocket (10)

All pattern products price under TCGplayer sub_type 'Holofoil'.

title: Ingest Pokémon Japan sets from TCGCSV
description: TCGCSV exposes Pokémon Japan as categoryId=85 with 447 groups (vs. category 3 = English Pokémon, which is what we ingest today). Every Japanese set is available with rich extendedData per product (rarity, HP, card type, weakness, attacks). Prices flow through the same /<group_id>/prices endpoint. No pokemontcg.io equivalent — Japanese cards must be synthesized from TCGCSV alone (similar to what synthesize_cards_for_bridges already does for English sets missing from pokemontcg.io). Goal: make Japanese sets and their cards first-class in the catalog so the user can enter Japanese copies via the same /browse + /card flows as English. Confirmed live during pokedumpster-bvi follow-up: the user owns Japanese vintage from at least 4 sets (Mystery of the Fossils, Gold/Silver To a New World, City Gym Decks, Leaders Stadium).
design:
Phase 1 — TcgcsvClient: thread a category_id parameter through fetch_groups/fetch_products/fetch_prices (default 3 = English). Configurable list of category IDs to import; setup/refresh hits each in turn.

Phase 2 — Card synthesis: extend synthesize_cards_for_bridges (or add a JP-specific synthesizer) to build cards table rows from TCGCSV product.extendedData. Mapping: name → cards.name, productId → cards.tcgplayer_product_id (via printings), Rarity → cards.rarity, HP → cards.hp, CardType → cards.types (single-element JSON array), Description → cards.flavor_text (or attacks JSON for Pokémon cards). Stage → subtypes. Etc.

Phase 3 — Set rows: synthesize sets entries with set_code convention 'jp-<slug>' or 'jp-<group_id>'. series field: bucket Japanese sets into era buckets ('Pokemon JP - WOTC era', 'Pokemon JP - DP/Platinum', 'Pokemon JP - Sword & Shield', 'Pokemon JP - Scarlet & Violet', 'Pokemon JP - Mega Evolution') by date or by group naming patterns. release_date from group.publishedOn.

Phase 4 — Variants: Japanese rarities map to additional variant codes (AR / Art Rare, SAR / Special Art Rare, CSR / Character Super Rare, CHR / Character Rare, HR / Hyper Rare, SR / Special Rare, UR / Ultra Rare). Either expand data/variants.json + tcgcsv_sub_type_variant_map, or let unrecognized sub_types fall through to missing_variant initially and patch as needed.

Phase 5 — UI: browse page already groups by series, so JP sets naturally appear under their JP-era buckets. Card detail / binder should Just Work. Spot-check whitespace and length issues with Japanese set names.

Estimated total effort: ~8-12h for full Japan catalog; ~3-4h if scoped to a hand-picked list of Japanese sets (config-driven import allowlist).
acceptance_criteria:
- pkdump data refresh / setup ingests both category 3 (English) and category 85 (Japanese Pokémon).
- Japanese sets appear on /browse under appropriate series buckets.
- Japanese cards have card detail pages with their printings, market prices, and 'add copy' flow working end-to-end.
- The 15 Japanese vintage cards the user identified during the bulk-lot offer work are reachable and addable through the standard UI.

title: Variant provenance: show what product/source each variant comes from
description:
When viewing a card modal (\`VariantModal.svelte\`) or the card detail page (\`CardDetailView.svelte\`), each variant chip/row should make it possible to tell what product the variant came from — e.g. a stamp_buildbattle printing came from a Build & Battle Box, a stamp_trick_or_trade printing came from "Trick or Trade BOOster Bundle 2023", a pokeball_rh came from a 151 booster pack, etc.

Today the user sees the variant label ("Master Ball Reverse Holo", "Trick or Trade Stamp") but no indication of which sealed product / event / promo channel originally distributed that printing. Ideal: a link to a sealed product (when one exists in our \`sealed_products\` table) or an external source URL; minimum bar: a short textual description.

Examples worth handling well:
- \`pokeball_rh\` / \`masterball_rh\` on a 151 card → "From the 151 booster (Poké Ball / Master Ball pattern reverse holo)"
- \`stamp_buildbattle\` → "From the [set]'s Build & Battle Box"
- \`stamp_trick_or_trade\` → "From the Trick or Trade BOOster Bundle [year]"
- \`stamp_black_bolt\` → "From a Black Bolt prerelease event"
- Anything attached via the MCAP cross-group bridge → resolves to the MCAP product's name verbatim
- Anything sourced from a Mega Evolution Premium Collection box → "Mega Zygarde Ex Premium Collection" (user's example)
design:
This is fundamentally a data-model question: where does provenance live? Two reasonable shapes.

**Option A: per-variant template, set/category-aware.** Add a \`provenance_template\` column to \`variants\` (or a sibling table keyed by variant_code) that gives a humane label, optionally templated on set/year context. Display layer just renders. Example: variant \`stamp_trick_or_trade\` → template "Trick or Trade BOOster Bundle {year}", with the year derived from the printing's tcgcsv group_id (group 3179 = 2022, 23266 = 2023, 23561 = 2024).

Pros: covers the common case (one stamp = one product story) with very little data.
Cons: doesn't capture per-card provenance (e.g. card X was specifically in box Y), but the user's example ("Mega Zygarde Ex Premium Collection") is product-level, not card-level — so this shape probably suffices.

**Option B: link printings to sealed_products.** Add an optional FK from \`printings\` to \`sealed_products\` (a printing was distributed via this sealed product). When set, the UI can render the sealed product name + link to its detail page (and to TCGplayer via \`tcgplayer_url\`). When unset, fall back to a variant-template description.

Pros: real entity linking, supports external URLs, scales to "this exact card came from this exact box".
Cons: needs a curated mapping somewhere — TCGCSV's sealed_products table has the box, but the products → cards link isn't a 1:1 anywhere. Would need a hand-curated overlay or per-variant default.

Recommend starting with **Option A** as the MVP (covers ~all sealed-product / stamp / pattern variants with one column), then layering Option B later if per-printing provenance becomes needed.

Concrete first pass:
1. Add \`provenance\` text column to \`variants\` (or a separate \`variant_provenance.json\` seed if we want to keep the variants table lean — matches CLAUDE.md's "data IS the product" pattern).
2. Seed it for the common variants: pokeball_rh, masterball_rh, all stamps, cosmos_holo, cosmos_holo_trick_or_trade, the various other reverse holos.
3. Add a \`provenance\` field to the printing API response (or compute it client-side from the typed variants registry already loaded via \`$lib/variants.svelte\`).
4. In VariantModal + CardDetailView, render the provenance as a small subtitle under each variant row.

Template substitution: keep it minimal — \`{set_name}\`, \`{year}\` (from a printing → tcgcsv_group_id → group year lookup). If a template wants something else, expand the substitution map later.
acceptance_criteria:
- Both VariantModal and CardDetailView render a short provenance line under each variant.
- All variants with a single canonical product source (stamps, ball patterns, cosmos holo, etc.) have a meaningful description.
- Variants without a known source (e.g. plain \`holo\` from old-era booster packs) gracefully render no provenance line, not a placeholder.
- New data lives in a seed file or table column, not switched in TS/Rust code (matches the data-IS-the-product convention in CLAUDE.md).
- Optional but nice: when a sealed product is identifiable, link to it (internal detail page or external TCGplayer URL).
close_reason: Closed

title: Browse index (/browse): add base-set progress bar to each set tile
description:
Today the /browse index renders one progress bar per set tile showing \`owned_cards / total_cards\` (\`frontend/src/routes/browse/+page.svelte:53-54\`) — the full master count, including secret rares, subsets, and promos. User wants an additional bar that tracks "do I have a copy of all numbered, non-secret cards?" — i.e. cards whose \`number_sortable <= printed_total\`.

The backing logic already exists for the per-set stats page: \`crates/pkdump-db/src/sets.rs:154-172\` (\`analytics()\`) computes \`base_total_cards\` / \`base_owned_cards\` using the predicate \`s.printed_total IS NOT NULL AND c.number_sortable <= s.printed_total\`. Mirroring this into \`list_sets()\` is the cleanest path — same SQL pattern, two more correlated subqueries.

\`SetSummary\` (\`crates/pkdump-db/src/sets.rs:11\`) needs two new fields: \`base_total_cards\`, \`base_owned_cards\`. Both \`#[ts(type = "number")]\` so the TS bindings update on next \`cargo test\`.
design:
**Backend.** Extend \`list_sets()\` SQL with two correlated subqueries matching \`analytics()\` (same predicate). Add \`base_total_cards\` / \`base_owned_cards\` to \`SetSummary\`. \`cargo test\` regenerates \`frontend/src/lib/types/SetSummary.ts\`.

**Frontend.** Each tile already has a \`.bar\`. Stack a second bar below the first; label the existing one "Master" and the new one "Base" (or visually distinguish them with the same color treatment used on the per-set page header — green-ish for base, red/pink for master). Total tile height grows slightly; the \`auto-fill, minmax(190px, 1fr)\` grid will reflow automatically.

The existing per-set \`/browse/<set>\` page already shows both bars in its header (\`frontend/src/routes/browse/[set]/+page.svelte:295-308\`), so the visual language is established — match it.
acceptance_criteria:

- Each tile on /browse shows both bars (Base and Master) with their counts.
- Sets where \`printed_total\` is NULL (some older promo sets, MEP, etc.) show "—" or hide the Base bar gracefully — no NaN%.
- A new backend test asserts the base counts are populated and match \`analytics()\`.

title: Collection table: variant/status tags pushed to right edge when card name wraps
description:
On /collection, the .namecell is a flex row containing the thumbnail, the card name \`\`, and the inline variant + status tags (e.g. "R" for Reverse Holo, "H" for Holofoil). When the card name fits on a single line, the tags abut the right edge of the name — natural left-aligned cluster. When the name is long enough to wrap to two lines, the tags get pushed to the right edge of the cell instead of continuing to abut the name. Cause: in \`frontend/src/routes/collection/+page.svelte:1566\` (\`.namecell { display: flex; align-items: center; }\`) the cardname span is a flex sibling of the tags. When its content would overflow, default \`flex-shrink: 1\` shrinks the span to whatever width remains after \`thumb + tags + gaps\`, forcing the text to wrap. The shrunken width is, by construction, equal to "available width minus tags", so the tag siblings land at the right edge of the cell. Markup at \`frontend/src/routes/collection/+page.svelte:867-884\`: \`\`\`svelte
… {a.name} … …
\`\`\`
design:
Wrap the cardname + tags in a single inline child of the flex row. Inside that wrapper they flow as inline content — when the name wraps, the tags follow the last line naturally and stay glued to the name. \`\`\`svelte
… {a.name}{#if a.variant !== 'normal'}…{/if}{#if statusBadge(a.status)}…{/if}
\`\`\` CSS: \`.namebody { min-width: 0; }\` and ensure \`.tag\` is \`display: inline-block; vertical-align: middle\` so the small letter-tags keep their pill shape while flowing inline. Verify by widening "Antique Cover Fossil" or similar long-named entry in the browser at small viewport width and confirming tags abut the wrapped name, not the cell's right edge.
acceptance_criteria:
- For both single-line and wrapped card names, the variant/status tags appear immediately after the last word of the name (left-clustered with the name), not at the cell's right edge.
- No visual regression on the other \`.namecell\` usage (line 964 — no tags, thumb + cardname only).

title: upstream_card_corrections: re-apply override to already-ingested rows
description:
\`data/overrides/upstream_card_corrections.json\` is applied inside \`upsert_card\` (\`crates/pkdump-ingest/src/pokemon_tcg_data.rs\`). That covers any newly-ingested row, but adding a new entry today does NOT heal a row that's already in the catalog — \`pkdump data refresh\`'s \`import_tail\` skips sets that already exist (\`crates/pkdump-cli/src/data.rs:142\` — \`if exists { continue; }\`), so existing cards are never re-upserted on the nightly path.

Concrete: when pokedumpster-fxb landed, the \`zsv10pt5-80\` row had to be healed with a one-time SQL UPDATE on prod because \`pkdump data refresh\` did not re-run \`upsert_card\` against it. The override is correct for any future ingest of that card, but the existing row needed manual intervention.

This is fine when the registry has exactly one entry. It becomes annoying if corrections accumulate (or if a correction is edited later) because every change would require a manual heal in prod.
design:
Add \`pkdump data apply-corrections [--dry-run]\` to the CLI. Walks every entry in \`upstream_card_corrections.json\`, and for each \`card_id\` that already exists in the \`cards\` table, applies the field-level overrides via UPDATE (and recomputes \`number_sortable\` when \`number\` is overridden). Idempotent — re-running is a no-op once rows match. \`--dry-run\` prints the rows that would change without writing.

Where the code goes:
- New \`fn apply_corrections(args)\` in \`crates/pkdump-cli/src/data.rs\` next to the existing \`refresh\` entrypoint.
- Re-use the override loader from \`crates/pkdump-ingest/src/pokemon_tcg_data.rs\` — extract \`upstream_card_corrections()\` to a small \`pub fn\` if needed, or factor a tiny \`apply_corrections_to_db(conn) -> usize\` next to it that the CLI calls.
- The healing SQL mirrors what \`upsert_card\` writes: \`UPDATE cards SET number = ?, number_sortable = ?\` (using \`pkdump_core::number_sortable\` for the sortable value), \`raw_json\` left untouched per existing convention.

Optional but probably worth it: also call \`apply_corrections_to_db\` as a final phase of \`pkdump data refresh\` so the next nightly heals any row whose override was added between runs. Cost is one SELECT per override entry — negligible.

Fail-first test: insert a card row with the wrong field value, run \`apply_corrections_to_db\`, assert the field updated to the corrected value and \`number_sortable\` recomputed. A second run is a no-op.
acceptance_criteria:
- \`pkdump data apply-corrections\` exists, walks the override registry, UPDATEs every matching \`cards\` row.
- \`--dry-run\` reports planned changes without writing.
- Either the new subcommand runs as part of \`pkdump data refresh\`, or there's a clear operator note telling the user to run it after adding an override.
- Fail-first test covers: corrected field is applied; \`number_sortable\` follows; second run is a no-op; non-matching card_ids are skipped.
- pokedumpster-fxb's prod heal becomes reproducible: run the subcommand against any catalog and the \`zsv10pt5-80\` row converges to \`number='80'\`.

title: Synthesize cards rows for bridged TCGCSV groups with no pokemontcg.io counterpart
description:
After pokedumpster-1x0 the MEP set tile renders in /browse, but clicking it opens an empty set — the 'cards' table has zero rows for set_code='mep' because pokemontcg.io has no upstream MEP set entry. TCGCSV has 83 product rows in group 24451 with enough data to synthesize bare-bones card rows so the binder grid actually populates.

Same shape would apply to any future synthesize-style bridge entry.

Out of scope for pokedumpster-1x0 (which delivered the set-tile bridge); this is the follow-up to make the bridged tile useful.
design:
TCGCSV product fields available per MEP card:
  - product_id  → tcgplayer_product_id (drives printings + prices)
  - name        → 'Meganium - 001' / 'Alakazam - 003 [Staff]' / 'Alakazam - 003 (Pokemon Center Exclusive)'
  - collector_number → '001' / '003' (variant treatments share the number)
  - image_url   → small/large image

Minimum to produce a usable card row:
  - card_id = '{set_code}-{number}' (e.g. 'mep-1', 'mep-3')
  - name    = parse_product_card_name (strips ' - 001' suffix and any trailing parenthetical/staff tag)
  - number, number_sortable
  - image_small / image_large from TCGCSV image_url
  - rarity = NULL (TCGCSV does not carry this)

Implementation likely lives in a new ingest module run during 'pkdump setup' / 'data refresh' after the bridge synthesis step. Idempotent — INSERT OR IGNORE on (card_id) keyed by collector_number per set_code, then variant expansion (now scanning the synthesized set's group via the existing own-group path in pkdump-ingest/src/overrides.rs:151) creates printings from the same products that justify the cards row.

Bridge entries opt in via a new 'synthesize_cards: true' flag on their entry in data/overrides/tcgcsv_set_bridges.json — SVP doesn't need it (pokemontcg.io provides cards), MEP does.
acceptance_criteria:
- After data refresh: cards table has one row per unique collector_number in TCGCSV group 24451.
- /browse/mep renders a populated binder grid with images.
- Cards picked up from TCGCSV (no upstream pokemontcg.io entry) are marked clearly so a future upstream-arrival merge is mechanical.
- Idempotent: re-running data refresh doesn't duplicate or drift the synthesized rows.
notes: Filed as the follow-up to pokedumpster-1x0. The bridge framework is already in place; this is the cards-population half.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 855c532 — synthesize_cards_for_bridges populates MEP from TCGCSV products. V3 migration adds tcgcsv_products.image_url; import_products now also derives stamp variants so own-group [Staff]/(Prerelease) products resolve correctly. Verified against prod DB copy: 60 cards created from 83 products. Images and full printings will populate on the next production data refresh.

title: Pre-LC variants: 1st Edition, Shadowless, Wizards-promo holo/non-holo not modelled

1. 1st Edition vs Unlimited — base1..base5 + gym1/gym2 + neo1..neo4 all shipped in 1st Edition and Unlimited print runs. KNOWN_VARIANTS already has first_ed_holo / first_ed_normal / unlimited_holo, but layer-1 needs pokemontcg.io price-key support (1stEditionHolofoil / 1stEditionNormal / unlimitedHolofoil) AND/OR overlay rules per set+rarity.

None of these block anyone today — pkdump has no users tracking pre-LC cards. File so the audit history is here when someone does.

Adding these would require ingesting pokemontcg.io's tcgplayer.prices keys as a secondary source AND a way to price the resulting printings (pokemontcg.io carries the prices but they don't map to a TCGCSV product_id, so the prices table schema would need to accept a non-TCGCSV source). title: TTBB 'Gengar (YYYY Copyright Date)' products don't bridge — 2 of 90 unresolved
description:
Two TTBB products didn't attach to a parent card on the first refresh after the bn9 bridge landed:

\`\`\`
3179  | 283766 | Gengar (2021 Copyright Date) | 057/198  (TTBB 2022)
23266 | 515661 | Gengar (2022 Copyright Date) | 066/196  (TTBB 2023)
\`\`\`

These are reprint markers ("2021 Copyright Date"/"2022 Copyright Date" parentheticals indicate which print run a given Gengar reprint came from). The bridge's parenthetical parser (\`variant_from_product_name\`) returns None for these strings — they're not a known variant pattern — so the products fall through the if-let chain and are skipped (the TTBB plain-name branch requires \`!name.contains('(')\`).

Two reasonable fixes:
1. Strip "(YYYY Copyright Date)" specifically and route to \`stamp_trick_or_trade\` like the bare-name TTBB products.
2. Recognize "(YYYY Copyright Date)" as a stand-alone variant code (e.g. \`reprint_2021\`) — but copyright-date isn't really a variant in the same sense as a stamp; it's just a print-run disambiguator that distinguishes near-identical TCGplayer SKUs.

Option (1) is cleaner — the user owns "Gengar with a Trick or Trade stamp", the print-run year is incidental.

Scope: 2 cards out of 90 in the TTBB chain. Not blocking.

value: Data model is the product. Anything data-shaped (lookups, labels, ranks, enums, derived display metadata) living in API or frontend code is a smell — flag it immediately. The schema is what lets UI tweaks stay simple and lets edge cases (which will surface as the collection is entered in anger) get fixed in one place. Bias toward: define it as a table or seed file, attach an FK, let display code do nothing but render. Examples found in May 2026: variantLabel/variantRank/variantColor/variantTag scattered across TS while the canonical variant list lived in a Rust constant — fixed by moving to shared.sqlite variants table (pokedumpster-mk4).
